title: Pricing concession automation & marketplace reconciliation triage
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Problem statement: As enterprise customers scale commitments and marketplace transactions, finance and account teams manually triage pricing concessions, invoice adjustments, and marketplace offsets. This leads to delayed credits, inconsistent cost allocation, and increased ops overhead. Goal: define an intake and decision framework plus implement automation rules for routine concession approvals and a reconciliation flow for marketplace offsets so that >80% of routine requests are resolved without manual finance intervention and end-to-end SLA for high-priority disputes is 3 business days.

Scope: pricing concessions (credits, one-time discounts, contract adjustments), marketplace reconciliation (seller/partner offsets, marketplace credit mapping), invoice reissuance triggers, and cost allocation tags for chargeback/ledger. Non-scope: legal contract renegotiations, tax adjustments requiring external counsel.

Deliverables: 1) triage rubric for intake and priority scoring, 2) set of deterministic automation rules (approve/route/escalate), 3) reconciliation playbook for marketplace offsets with audit trail and ledger mapping, 4) dashboards and alerts for exceptions, 5) runbook for Finance/Support handoff.
updates: 2025-02-10 — Ticket created by Ava Moreno: initial problem framing and goals attached.

2025-02-14 — Kickoff meeting: Attendees: PM (Ava), Eng (Priya Patel), Finance (Derek Mullins), Support (Nora Li). Agreed success metrics and ownership. Action: Eng to prototype rules engine feasibility (batch vs event-driven).

2025-02-21 — Prototype review: Priya demoed a rules engine sketch using existing tagging service; two canonical rules proposed: (1) concession <= $5k and <15% discount auto-approve with audit; (2) marketplace offset < $10k route to Finance queue with pre-populated reconciliation payload. Decision: expand exception metadata to include 'contract_commitment_id' and 'marketplace_txn_id'.
2025-02-27 — PM review with Finance: Derek requested auditability for approvals and an override flow. Added requirement: approval/action must produce immutable record (ticket + ledger event id).

2025-03-02 — Status: Design docs in draft and linked; assigned Eng epic ENG-41280 for implementation. Next: finalize triage rubric and acceptance criteria, start implementation spike for ledger mapping APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form and API accept required fields: customer_id, contract_commitment_id (optional), requested_amount_usd, reason_code, priority_hint, marketplace_txn_id (optional)
Automated rule engine executes on intake and returns one of: auto-approve, route-to-finance, escalate-to-legal, request-more-info
Auto-approve rules resolve and emit credit event to ledger service with audit ID; downstream invoice adjustments are scheduled within 48 hours
Exceptions (route-to-finance) create a pre-populated Finance task with reconciliation payload and SLA 3 business days
Dashboard surfaces daily counts: total intakes, auto-approved %, routed, average resolution latency; alert if auto-approve rate drops >15% week-over-week
All produced artifacts (approval records, ledger events) are queryable by Finance/Support and have immutable timestamps and operator IDs
implementation_notes: Use existing tagging and ledger APIs where possible; ENG spike to document missing payload fields (ENG-41280)
Rule engine should be configurable via a policy table stored in Config Service (non-code changes for thresholds)
Provide a sandbox mode exposing decision trace for QA and Finance (simulate mode that does not emit ledger events)
Add a lightweight UI in the Console 'Billing > Requests' for Finance to view and take actions; initial MVP can be a filtered Support dashboard linking to Finance tickets
Telemetry: event names — billing.request.created, billing.request.decision, billing.request.ledger_emitted, billing.request.escalated
Fallback: if ledger write fails, mark request as 'needs-retry' and create Finance task; retries should be idempotent
